question:
A function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ is defined by $f(1)=f(2)=1$ and $f(n)=n-1$ for every natural number $n>2$. The rule is designed so that the first two inputs share an output, while all later inputs are shifted down by one. Students investigate how these features affect injectivity and surjectivity. Since the codomain is the complete set of natural numbers, they must check whether every natural number is obtained, including $1$. They must also distinguish between the failure of uniqueness of pre-images and the existence of at least one pre-image.

(a) Find $f(1)$, $f(2)$, $f(5)$ and $f(10)$.

(b) Determine whether $f$ is one-one and justify your answer.

(c) For any $y\in\mathbb{N}$ with $y>1$, find an input $n$ such that $f(n)=y$.

(d) Explain why $1$ also has a pre-image and hence determine whether $f$ is onto.
explanation:
(a)
By definition, $f(1)=1$ and $f(2)=1$. Since $5>2$, $f(5)=5-1=4$. Since $10>2$, $f(10)=10-1=9$.

(b)
The two distinct inputs $1$ and $2$ have the same image because $f(1)=f(2)=1$. Therefore, $f$ is not one-one.

(c)
Let $y\in\mathbb{N}$ with $y>1$. Choose $n=y+1$. Then $n>2$, so $f(n)=n-1=(y+1)-1=y$. Therefore, every natural number greater than $1$ has a pre-image.

(d)
The natural number $1$ has pre-images $1$ and $2$, since $f(1)=f(2)=1$. By part (c), every natural number greater than $1$ also has a pre-image. Therefore, every element of the codomain $\mathbb{N}$ has at least one pre-image, so $f$ is onto. Thus, the function is onto but not one-one.

options.A: $f(1)=1$, $f(2)=2$, $f(5)=4$ and $f(10)=9$; $f$ is one-one but not onto because $1$ has no pre-image.
options.B: $f(1)=1$, $f(2)=1$, $f(5)=4$ and $f(10)=9$; $f$ is not one-one, every $y>1$ has the pre-image $y+1$, and $1$ has the pre-images $1$ and $2$. Hence, $f$ is onto.
options.C: $f(1)=f(2)=1$, $f(5)=5$ and $f(10)=10$; $f$ is both one-one and onto because every natural number has exactly one pre-image.
options.D: $f(1)=f(2)=1$, $f(5)=4$ and $f(10)=9$; $f$ is neither one-one nor onto because the image $1$ has two pre-images.
